articles.title: What Is an MVP and How Much Should It Cost?
articles.excerpt: MVP development cost explained in plain terms: what an MVP includes, what drives the price, and how to scope a first version that proves your idea. If you have an idea for an app or a web platform, yo…
articles.body: MVP development cost explained in plain terms: what an MVP includes, what drives the price, and how to scope a first version that proves your idea. If you have an idea for an app or a web platform, you have probably heard the advice to build an MVP first. The advice is sound. The confusing part is what those three letters mean in practice, and what you should expect to pay. MVP stands for minimum viable product. It is the smallest version of your product that real users can try, use, and give honest feedback on. It is not a demo or a slide deck. It is a working product, just a focused one. MVP development cost is the question almost every founder asks next, and it has the widest range of answers.

articles.title: The Hidden Cost of Poor API Design in Modern Web Applications
articles.excerpt: An API can work perfectly during initial development and still become one of the biggest obstacles to an application's growth. Poor API design rarely causes immediate failure. Instead, it creates prob…
articles.body: An API can work perfectly during initial development and still become one of the biggest obstacles to an application's growth. Poor API design rarely causes immediate failure. Instead, it creates problems that become increasingly expensive as applications gain features, users, and integrations. Frontend developers start adding workarounds, backend changes become risky, and even simple improvements require modifications across multiple components. Poor API design increases development time, creates unnecessary frontend complexity, and makes applications harder to maintain and scale. The real cost is not always the API itself, but the engineering effort required to work around its limitations. 1.

articles.title: Gemini Decision 1 and Decider v1.3: A Decision Layer in Front of Your Agent
articles.excerpt: Quick summary: Google released the Gemini Decisions API on November 11, and Perplexity followed with open weights for Decider v1.3 the next day. Both separate decisions over fixed options from text ge…
articles.body: Quick summary: Google released the Gemini Decisions API on November 11, and Perplexity followed with open weights for Decider v1.3 the next day. Both separate decisions over fixed options from text generation, making them useful for routing, checks, and filtering before an agent runs. What matters is more than skipping a written response: it is a single forward pass, question isolation, and thresholds you can calibrate. This article covers how they work, the tradeoffs between hosted and self-hosted deployment, and code that decides first and calls a generative model only when needed. 1.

articles.body: 2016년, 더 다오(The DAO) 해킹 사건이 터져 약 360만 이더리움(ETH)이 사라졌을 때, 나는 이 분야를 오랫동안 지켜봐 온 우리 모두가 숨을 헙 들이켰던 순간을 기억한다. 단순히 해킹 사건이 아니었다. 코드가 결함투성이일 때 "코드는 곧 법"이라는 잔혹한 현실을 일깨워준 심오하고도 초기적인 교훈이었다. 그때 나를 강하게 사로잡았던 것, 그리고 오늘날까지도 깊이 공감하는 바는, 기술이 눈부신 속도로 발전했음에도 스마트 계약 보안의 근본적인 문제들이 결국 인간의 실수와 시스템적인 허점으로 귀결된다는 점이다. 수십 년간 쌓아온 나의 관점은 이것이 한 번에 "해결"되는 문제가 아니라는 것이다. 이는 끊임없이 진화하는 싸움이며, 오래된 취약점이 패치되는 속도만큼이나 빠르게 새로운 공격 벡터가 출현한다. 문제는 단순히 코드에만 있지 않다. 설계와 감사부터 배포, 그리고 지속적인 감시에 이르는 전체 라이프사이클에 걸쳐 존재한다. 배경 더 다오 사건은 겉보기에 미묘한 코딩 결함이 어떻게 치명적인 손실로 이어질 수 있는지를 생생하게 보여주는 뼈아픈 교훈으로 남아 있다. 공격자는 재진입(reentrancy) 취약점을 악용했는데, 이는 외부 계약에 대한 호출이 원래 계약의 상태가 업데이트되기 전에 "재진입"할 수 있는 메커니즘이다. ATM에서 돈을 인출하는데, 잔고가 차감되기도 전에 또 다른 인출을 시작할 수 있다고 상상해 보라. 본질적으로 이런 일이 일어난 것이다. 공격자는 withdrawRewardFor 함수를 반복적으로 호출하여 자금을 빼돌렸다.

articles.title: 'Don't panic': SpaceX pens familiar message on Starship ahead of historic double-catch test flight
articles.excerpt: SpaceX has inked a familiar phrase on the Starship rocket that will fly a historic mission today (Nov. 13) — "Don't panic." And the company has invoked those words before.
articles.body: SpaceX has a message for itself, and for the spacecraft set to make history today (Nov. 13): Don't panic. The company's Starship megarocket will conduct its 15th test flight this afternoon, a landmark liftoff that will feature the first-ever attempt to catch both of its stages with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms. On Thursday (Nov. 12), SpaceX rolled the Flight 15 upper stage, a vehicle known as Ship 42, out to the launch pad at its Starbase site in South Texas to prep. The company shared photos of the move on X , and in two of those shots we can see some intriguing words inked on the spacecraft: "Don't panic." Another look at Ship 42 at the pad on Nov. 12.

articles.title: Netflix's Disappointing New Western Thriller Wastes Its Brilliant Concept
articles.excerpt: Netflix’s Heartland is a western, a noir, and a musical starring Jessica Chastain. It’s also surprisingly predictable.
articles.body: Written and directed by Shana Feste, the Netflix-original film feels as if the director of Country Strong watched a couple of episodes of Yellowstone and decided to take a stab at a western-noir, centering her story on a jaded country star. The result is a missing-person mystery with three musical numbers woven into it. Heartland might be the first western-noir-musical ever made, and I wish Feste took advantage of how weird that is. Instead, it’s pure straight-to-Netflix fodder.

Grok Bot can already call consenting individuals, while Google is exploring similar capabilities for Gemini. Google’s Gemini has already learned to sit through hold music, navigate phone menus, and speak to businesses on your behalf. The feature even expanded to Pixel 10 phones this week. Now, Meta wants its own AI assistant to take those unwanted calls off your hands. Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, announced on X that Muse can now make outgoing calls for paid subscribers in the US.

articles.title: 26 Years Later, Charles Schulz' Final Comic Strip Is Still an All-Time Peanuts Classic
articles.excerpt: 26 Years Later, Charles Schulz' Final Comic Strip Is Still an All-Time Peanuts Classic
articles.body: While that was the first official Peanuts comic, a similar version by Charles Schulz predated Peanuts and ran in Minnesota’s St. Paul Pioneer Press. It was called Li’l Folks and also starred cute little children, although it did not have a regular cast like Peanuts would. Li’l Folks ran from 1947 until 1950, when Schulz quit after his editor refused to give him a raise from the $10 per comic he was making. After that, Schulz brought Li’l Folks to United Feature Syndicate. The national cartoon syndicator liked the comic, but needed to change its name because of a 1930s comic strip called Little Folks .

articles.excerpt: Let your data do the talking, without revealing everything else.
articles.body: TL;DR Google Sheets now lets users publish Gemini-powered Canvas dashboards, calendars, and task boards through shareable links. People can interact with a published Canvas without accessing or editing the original spreadsheet. Users can control who sees the Canvas and choose whether it updates automatically when spreadsheet data changes. Google Sheets is great for organizing information, but sharing it with others isn’t always convenient. Say you’re managing a project with multiple deadlines and tasks. You might have everything organized in a spreadsheet, but no one wants to scroll through dozens of rows just to see what’s happening next. Google already has a feature called Canvas that uses Gemini to turn spreadsheet data into interactive dashboards, calendars, and task boards.

articles.body: SpaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live. Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). SpaceX plans to bring both of Starship's stages back to Starbase for a catch by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — something it has never done before. You can watch it all live here at Space.com. And there should be a lot to see: Starship Flight 15 will last more than 22 hours, if all goes according to plan. articles.title: 'Man of Tomorrow': Release date, plot, cast & everything we know about the 'Superman' sequel
articles.excerpt: James Gunn's new DC universe might be done, but the follow-up to 2025's Superman is still on the way.
articles.body: It feels like yesterday when we were discussing Superman , the first big-screen entry in James Gunn's rebooted DCU. Now Gunn is out , and Skydance (the company formed by the merger of Warner and Paramount) is already dismantling his grand plans for the DCU. That means that Man of Tomorrow, which arrives next summer, will be the final entry in Gunn's ambitious, and occasionally divisive, DC experiment. The DCU's first chapter — officially titled 'Gods and Monsters' — gave us Supergirl and Clayface (as well as TV shows like Peacemaker S2 and Lanterns ) in the run-up to Clark Kent and Lex Luthor 's return.

articles.title: This supernova impostor baffled astronomers for 15 years — until they found a hidden black hole feeding on an unstable star
articles.excerpt: A hidden black hole or neutron star companion to an unstable massive star is causing the system to erupt in light that mimics a supernova explosion.
articles.body: A cosmic imposter that has faked being a supernova 27 times and counting is actually a hot, luminous, and decidedly unstable star that is being fed on by a vampiric black hole or neutron star, NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory has discovered. When a massive star reaches the end of the road and runs out of nuclear fuel to power fusion reactions in its core, the star is destroyed in a supernova explosion. That’s what astronomers thought they had found on 11 January 2012, when they observed what appeared to be a supernova on the outskirts of the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, which is about 25 million light-years away in the constellation Coma Berenices. Yet when the light of the 'supernova' faded, the star was still there, only to continue bursting into light every 113 days.
